nodes.rationale: interface.state is not None was true for any composite interface inheriting a stateful base via MRO, causing permanent silent no-op state subscriptions for composites like ICamera that never publish under their own name; has_own_state() checks '"state" in cls.__dict__' to distinguish owning a schema from merely inheriting one, fixing two call sites without redesigning the interface hierarchy.

nodes.label: ADR-0002: XMPP stream-error conflict quits instead of reconnecting
nodes.rationale: ejabberd's 'conflict' stream error is indistinguishable at the protocol level between an admin kick and a genuine JID takeover; auto-reconnecting on conflict just re-races whoever holds the resource, so the module quits instead, relying on an external supervisor to restart it. Distinguishing kick vs. takeover via the error's <text> was rejected since both warrant the same response.

nodes.label: ADR-0003: Restrict Proxy access to async with
nodes.rationale: Once Proxy carried live state kept current via a PubSub subscription, a long-lived stashed 'await self.proxy(...)' reference could silently go stale after the remote module disconnected/reconnected. Single-mode 'async with' removes the ability to hold a proxy indefinitely by construction; a dual-mode or explicit-lifecycle API would still rely on discipline at each call site.
nodes.norm_label: adr-0003: restrict proxy access to async with

nodes.label: ADR-0004: Enforce access control on the callee, not the caller
nodes.rationale: A caller-side allowlist is just the caller's own code and can be bypassed trivially by a bug, misconfiguration, or compromise; only the callee can make authorization stick, so an optional acl: config block is checked inside Module.execute() before dispatch, additive/backward-compatible like Interface.version defaulting to 1.

nodes.label: ADR-0005: IConfig stays a stringly-keyed fallback
nodes.rationale: IConfig's genericness is deliberate, not an oversight: it's the fallback for config values that haven't graduated into their own typed interface method or IStructuredConfig. Tightening it would collapse the distinction between generic and dedicated interfaces without gaining real type safety, since callers would still pass a name: str.

nodes.label: ADR-0006: Proxy.wait_for_state() returns None on timeout
nodes.rationale: Every caller of wait_for_state() already writes 'state = await proxy.wait_for_state(...)' followed by an 'is not None' check, implying a non-raising contract was already assumed everywhere. Confirmed by a real production TimeoutError in SunCamera's _publish_camera_state() turning an ordinary 'not published yet' case into an ERROR traceback every 5s; catching TimeoutError inside the method itself avoids auditing every call site individually.
nodes.norm_label: adr-0006: proxy.wait_for_state() returns none on timeout

nodes.label: ADR-0007: get_interfaces() waits before raising IndexError
nodes.rationale: A raw dict subscript on _interface_cache raised KeyError instantly for a peer whose presence hadn't been processed yet, indistinguishable from a genuinely missing peer, and bypassed _get_client()'s existing 'except IndexError: return None' path (mismatched exception type). Chosen: bounded poll (20 attempts, 0.25s = 5s total) before raising the already-documented IndexError, resolving the common startup race silently while still failing promptly for a truly offline peer.
nodes.norm_label: adr-0007: get_interfaces() waits before raising indexerror

nodes.label: ADR-0008: _safe_send keeps bounded retry unlike capability/subscribe fetches
nodes.rationale: _get_capabilities()/_subscribe_with_retry() run as detached background tasks with no caller awaiting them, so retrying indefinitely has no caller-visible cost and fixes a real bug (25cbaad2) where a slow peer permanently lost its fetch. _safe_send() is awaited synchronously from paths like Module.open(), where unbounded retry would risk hanging the module forever (the #664/#666 failure mode) instead of raising IqTimeout after a bounded budget. Jitter applies to all three regardless.
nodes.norm_label: adr-0008: _safe_send keeps bounded retry unlike capability/subscribe fetches

nodes.label: ADR-0009: Event-loop lag watchdog lives on Module
nodes.rationale: A pyobs-iag50 incident required slow manual cross-module log archaeology to confirm a stalled event loop was the cause of disco#info timeouts. Comm was rejected since the failure mode is generic, not transport-specific; Application was rejected because it lacks Object's add_background_task lifecycle (auto-start/cancel/restart, log tagging) for free. Module reuses that infrastructure and matches the existing background-task pattern. Logging is edge-triggered (start/clear) rather than per-check, to avoid spam during a sustained-but-fluctuating overload.
nodes.norm_label: adr-0009: event-loop lag watchdog lives on module

nodes.label: ADR-0010: pyobs-gui stays on QtWidgets, not QML
nodes.rationale: QML's declarative/reactive model would genuinely fit pyobs-gui's state-driven UI better, but migrating requires rewriting the Python-to-UI bridge across all 18 widgets with no automated GUI test suite, for a benefit that's mostly internal code quality rather than operator-visible. pyobs-gui keeps structural advantages regardless of UI framework (being a real Module with LocalComm/IFitsHeaderBefore, in-process astropy/sunpy computation) that a browser client (pyobs-web-client, or Electron-wrapped) cannot replicate.

nodes.label: PyObsError exception hierarchy
nodes.rationale: A PyObsError subclass survives the RPC round trip only if it lives in pyobs.utils.exceptions and is a PyObsError subclass; builtins, ad hoc classes, and vendor SDK exceptions silently degrade to generic RemoteError on the wire, discarding the original type. This is the structural reason vendor/third-party exceptions must be converted to a PyObsError before leaving the module that raised them.

nodes.label: register_exception()/handle_exception() (frequency-based escalation)
nodes.rationale: Fires at construction time via a metaclass, counts occurrences of an exception type (process-global state), and can substitute the exception for SevereError once a threshold is hit -- an emergent interaction with any per-instance logging-suppression mechanism, since escalation can silently change the type after logging was disabled for the original type.

nodes.label: _disable_exception_logging (proposed verbosity control)
nodes.rationale: Proposed as a per-Module-instance, isinstance-matched verbosity control read only in Module.execute()'s catch block -- distinct from register_exception's frequency-based circuit breaker, which operates at construction time and can change the exception's actual type via SevereError substitution.

nodes.label: pyobs-brot: _error_state() never raises (roof/dome/telescope)
nodes.rationale: BrotRoof/BrotDome/BrotBaseTelescope's shared _error_state() helper only logs and sets ERROR status; every calling init()/park() then returns successfully to the RPC caller even on genuine hardware failure, despite IMotion documenting Raises: InitError/ParkError -- the most serious gap found, since nothing crosses the RPC boundary at all rather than the wrong type crossing it.

nodes.label: External interfaces registry design (__init_subclass__)
nodes.rationale: Interface resolution was hardcoded against the pyobs.interfaces module namespace at three chokepoints, silently dropping external interfaces from advertisement entirely. An import-time _REGISTRY populated by Interface.__init_subclass__ fixes this; the purity filter must check registry membership (not issubclass(base, Interface)) to avoid registering concrete module classes like BaseCamera/DummyCamera as pseudo-interfaces -- a real bug caught by the test suite, not design review.

nodes.label: ICamera/IExposure decoupling design
nodes.rationale: ICamera(IData, IExposure) forced every implementer to carry ExposureState even when no exposure has real progress -- PipelineCamera publishes fabricated, never-updated ExposureState purely to satisfy the inherited contract. ICamera/ISpectrograph drop the IExposure base; modules with genuine exposure-progress semantics (BaseCamera, BaseSpectrograph) declare IExposure explicitly. Precedent: IVideo(IData) already gets a GUI widget (VideoWidget) without IExposure, and CameraWidget already feature-detects IExposure via has_proxy, so no GUI-side change is required.

nodes.label: IDataSequence: server-side counted data sequences design
nodes.rationale: Client-driven exposure-count loops (CameraWidget.expose()) die with the client's connection and cost N RPC round-trips. IDataSequence pairs with IData (not ICamera) since grab_data() itself lives on IData, so any IData device (camera, video, spectrograph) is a legitimate case. grab_sequence() returns immediately and runs as a background task so its own @timeout stays meaningful regardless of count, with progress observable via pushed DataSequenceState instead of one long end-to-end deadline.

nodes.label: Image.trim(): unify three TRIMSEC implementations
nodes.rationale: Three independent TRIMSEC-parsing implementations existed (ProjectedOffsets regex, fitssec(), Pipeline.trim_ccddata via ccdproc). A CCDData round-trip (to_ccddata/from_ccddata) loses Image's catalog/raw/meta fields and neither ccdproc nor the existing code ever adjusts CRPIX1/CRPIX2 for the new origin, so Image.trim() is implemented directly on Image (no CCDData round trip), reusing fitssec()'s parser, shifting CRPIX on trim, deleting TRIMSEC/DATASEC/BIASSEC from the header, and raising if a catalog is already attached rather than silently invalidating its pixel coordinates.
